data.narrative:
Tonbo Imaging is a Series D-stage defense and security company that has raised $66.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 10 companies—2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms in the same sector and stage, including Saronic ($9.2B), Quantum-Systems ($8.0B), Chaos Industries ($4.5B), True Anomaly ($2.2B), and Onebrief ($2.1B).

Two triangulation methods are applied. The Stage-Progression method uses total capital raised ($66.5M) as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical of Series D advancement, yielding $100M. The Peer-Median method benchmarks against the five same-sector, same-stage comparables listed above, with a median valuation of $4.5B and a range spanning $2.1B to $9.2B.

The analysis supports a broad valuation range of $85M to $5.2B, with a median point of $2.3B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty regarding Tonbo's competitive positioning and technology maturity relative to peers. The Stage-Progression method produces a substantially lower result than peer benchmarking, suggesting either that Tonbo trades at a discount to the comparable set or that peer valuations embody significant growth premiums not yet realized by the company. Capital efficiency and path to profitability remain key variables in narrowing this range.
